refSet.reason: 칩셋 bbox-village-ramps 의 화풍 기준 묶음이 없다

surfaces.part: stair steps in the centre (6 repeating bands of 8 rows)
grass cap on the cliff edge (left and right)
dirt cliff walls on the left and right sides
cobblestone floor at the foot of the stairs

answer.evidence: Each step repeats every 8 rows. Row 0, 8, 16 and so on is a bright nose line (L about 197-223), followed by a lighter-to-mid tread band of rows 1-4. Rows 5-7 are a dark L=63 shadow band, which acts as the riser and eave shadow. This repetition gives a tread plus edge line plus shadow structure on every step, not a flat front elevation. The grass at rows 0-2 caps the dirt cliff walls on both sides. The cliff section is about 48 rows tall, and the cobblestone floor from row 48 is flat ground. The dirt walls are vertical cliff faces, as expected for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate carries 10 visible tones per tile, above the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so no 5x5 area is a single flat colour. Only 17% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines lean brown or grey-green. They read as the dark tone of the adjacent wood and stone, not a black sticker line. The steps show about 5 lightness steps: a light lip highlight, a mid grey face, a darker underside shadow and a deep line. The wooden side posts have a light-to-dark grain ramp with grassy tops. The cobble cliff base below has per-stone shading in the same style as the paving reference. The steps are somewhat banded and regular, and the posts are a little smoother than the reference grain, so texture is 'some' rather than fully rich. A reviewer would still accept it next to the references.

Each step therefore has a roughly 5-row horizontal tread and a 3-row dark riser or shadow face below it. The dirt strips on the left and right are flat vertical cliff edges, not receding isometric side faces. The cobble floor at rows 48-63 is plain ground.

The column scans at x=16 and x=23 show this pattern, giving about 5 tread rows and 3 riser rows per step. The side strips are vertical dirt and sand faces, and the cobblestone floor below row 48 is flat ground. For terrain this is a 3/4 stair, though the front-edge line is not a distinct row.

surfaces.part: stair treads (5 stacked steps, each about 8 rows, light to mid-grey bands)
cobble floor at the stair foot

answer.evidence: Each step repeats the same pattern. Rows 8-13 are a light highlight line on top, then 4-5 mid-grey tread rows. Rows 14-15 form a dark shadow line with the dark riser below it, then the next highlight line at row 16 (the pattern repeats at rows 0-7, 16-23, 24-31, 32-39 and 40-47). So each step has about 5 rows of tread and about 3 rows of dark riser. The reading is ambiguous: the light line could instead be a nosing on a front-elevation riser. I read it as a tread with a front-edge line and eave shadow. The steps stack down to a cobbled floor at rows 48-63. Dirt walls on the left and right and a grass cap at the top frame the cut. No isometric side face is drawn.
